utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now could we show the witness the next photograph, and may it be given the next number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P110.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: While that's coming up, Mr. Karabeg, could you tell us what kind of activity went on at the administration building, the white building you pointed out to us in Exhibit number 108? What happened there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the administration building, that was where the guards had their headquarters centre. When they would beat us, although they beat us in the garages and the compound itself, but mostly when they beat us up in the evening, they would call us to come to the administration building one by one. They would call us out one by one to avoid having any witnesses, any eyewitnesses to the beatings. But what was characteristic was that when you were called out to go to the building alone and you would be beaten up and returned back to the garage, that same person, half an hour later, so if I was beaten alone, then he would come and ask sort of in a provocative way, "How are you? How do you feel? I don't want anybody beating you, and if anybody beats you, come to me and I'll protect you." And you just look at him and think, Well, you beat me up half an hour ago and now you're coming to ask me how I am and ask me whether anybody was beating me and whether I needed any help. But that was to intimidate us and, of course, they took us out one by one so they wouldn't have any eyewitnesses to the beatings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you please look at Exhibit P110 and tell us if you recognise what's depicted there.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the inside of one of the garages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And approximately how big was the garage in which you were kept?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The garage was three by five metres, perhaps six. I know it was three metres wide. Now, whether it was five or six metres long, I can't really say. I think it would be six metres more like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And during your detention there, what was the maximum number of individuals kept in that room at any one time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would be as many as 37 of us. When I was brought in, there were just four, because the previous group who was in the Betonirka was sent to the Manjaca camp. So that was the least number there ever was, but on an average there would be between 20 and 25 of us, but when a new lot came in there would be up to 37 of us at certain points in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of the people who were kept in there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Non-Serbs. Bosniaks and Croats, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you know, were they civilians or military personnel or some combination?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know where they were all from, what municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the detainees were from the area of the Sanski Most municipality. There were no other detainees, no other people from other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who were the people who were guarding you during your detention in the garages?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. They were not actually guarding us. They beat us and mistreated us, and all of them were members of the police force, members of the reserve police force as well, members of various working groups that they had, the SOS members, for instance, who would come in from time to time to beat myself and others who were detained in garages. But they were all from the territory of the Sanski Most municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of the police and the SSO -- the SOS members who were guarding you and beating you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to people -- well, you mention at one time there were as many as 37 people in your garage. Do you know what happened to those people after they were taken away from the garage where you stayed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, those who were taken out from the garage would be beaten up, and some of those who were taken out would then be sent to Manjaca, mostly to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, if we could show the witness the next exhibit. It's a document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could we show the witness the next exhibit, a document dated 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P111.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, you told us that some of the people were taken to Manjaca. How did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how. Normally they would round up the prisoners who would be then taken to Manjaca. I think that as far as the Sanski Most area is concerned, the detainees were taken to Manjaca on five different occasions. I was in the last group which consisted of 49 people. We were also taken to Manjaca. We knew that we would be taken to Manjaca. And I also saw the people who had been taken to Manjaca. I saw them there at Manjaca when I got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the document that's in front of you. The B/C/S is 00471274, and this appears to be some conclusions of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff. I want to ask you about number 1 and number 2. Number 1 indicates that three individuals are going to be in charge of resolving the issue of prisoners and their categorisation. The three categories are politicians, national extremists, and people unwelcome in Sanski Most municipality. At that time, were you aware of any kind of categorising of the prisoners that you were among?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I saw this for the first time the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And number 2 talks about the Crisis Staff decides to appoint Drago Vujanic, as prison warden. At the time you were in the prison behind the police station and at Betonirka, did you know who the warden was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the beginning at least. Because it was only later, after my arrival, that I learned that he was the -- the prison warden. I was there from the 25th of May until the 9th of June. He never came to see us, so I didn't know who the prison warden was. Actually, I thought that it is was Papric, because he was the one who visited me on the second day. But it was only once that I arrived in Betonirka that I learned that he was the warden and that Mico Krunic, a retired police officer, was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, may the next item be given an exhibit number and shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation, if I might formally for the record indicate that I will be objecting to this particular document because its provenance has not been established. Additionally, it's indicated in the English translation that certain matters are underlined and there's some circling, and it doesn't seem to be actually a translation of that particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hannis, I also noticed that under item 2 it says circled 3, whereas in the original I do not see any circled 3, as a matter of fact. Therefore, we have a similar problem here as we had previously. Apart from that, Ms. Loukas objects since these -- as she said, the provenance has not been established. Ms. Loukas, may I ask you before we continue that to look at the back at least of the second page of the B/C/S version and on the fourth page where at least we find some indication as far as the -- well, perhaps not a source but at least it's attested by Jutta Paczulla of the ICTY that is a copy is compared to the original and that -- I don't know whether you took that into account when you said you wanted to object, whether you would say that Jutta Paczulla should appear and testify about that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Just in relation to that, Your Honour, while it is noted that the document came from AID, we don't know how it got to AID. So in that sense the provenance has not been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay. Let's -- I noticed your objection at this moment. Mr. Hannis, would it be appropriate to find out during the next break a bit more details about it and then give you an opportunity, if you would have concluded your examination-in-chief until the next break to give you an opportunity to just put additional questions in relation to this document after you have given a clarification which satisfies the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will. I have no further questions for this witness about this document, and I can address that issue, but I will also address the issue you mentioned regarding the translation and the circling and underlying. I think it is similar to our problem from this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't remember if we asked to have the next document shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the Court would be so kind to allow me to say just a few words regarding item 2, very briefly, concerning this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, we have a procedural issue which we'd like to resolve first before we hear any further testimony in relation to this document. So I would ask you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. I wasn't going to testify about the document. I just wanted to tell you something about this particular category of nationalist extremists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked whether you knew anything about the categories, and I'd rather leave it to that time when -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I want to show you another document dated the 6th of June, and if it could be begin the next number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P112.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, this appears to be a letter from the acting chief of police in Sanski Most to the Manjaca military commander talking about an agreement regarding prisoners from Sanski Most to Manjaca, and I want to ask you about a remark in the last paragraph which states: "We're still holding several persons in the detention rooms in this public security station, and that we shall also send them to you for further procedure after the operative processing." You were being held in Sanski Most at the prison on June the 6th of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from your experience there during your that time, can you tell the Court what operative processing of prisoners consisted of?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, we were often beaten up, mistreated, humiliated, and of course in such situations we sometimes felt forced to admit to the things we had never done. So this was duress and coercion. They tried to force us to give statements, and then they would send us to Manjaca. There were 960 of us who were processed, so to speak, in the same way. I mean 960 from Sanski Most. So it was after a series of beatings and torture and ill-treatment that we were sent to Manjaca for further action. Interrogators came to Manjaca as well, and beatings continued there as well. They would take people out of the compound, out of the premises, the rooms there, and beat them up as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when were you taken to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how long did you remain there before you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 31st of October, 1992, when I was exchanged in Turbe near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Karabeg, I'm not going to ask you the details about your detention in Manjaca because we have some other witnesses who have talked about that. But I do want to ask you, while you were there, did you have occasion to talk with other detainees who had come to Manjaca from Sanski Most municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware from conversations with those other people about what was happening with regard to the non-Serb population in Sanski Most municipality in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. This is what we talked about most. There were two camps at Manjaca. They were separated with a fence, a wire fence. I was at the second camp where there were three barns where between 600 and 700 of us were located. Most of us were from Sanski Most, Prijedor, Kljuc, Kotor Varos, Jajce, Sipovo, and from other areas of the Banja Luka region. All of us non-Serbs, Bosnian Muslims, and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware of what was happening with the non-Serb population in Sanski Most municipality other than those of you who were detained? Were those people staying or leaving the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did receive some information to the effect that almost everyone, as a result of mistreatment, killings, beatings, arson, and plunder of non-Serb property, that the majority tried to leave as soon as possible. So this was all being done to them in order to force them to leave their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware of any requirements that were imposed by the Serb or the SDS authorities on non-Serbs to leave the municipality at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, this is how it was: Those people were mistreated in every possible way. The situation became untenable for them, and they tried to leave those parts as soon as they could. In order to be able to leave Sanski Most, they were all forced to sign a statement to the effect that they would never come back and that they were leaving all their movable and immovable property to the municipality, to the municipal authorities. And what is even more telling, they were forced to pay their electricity bills, water bills, various taxes, taxes on land, on business, on property. So they had to settle all of that and then they would sign a statement to the effect that they were leaving all their property to the municipal organs. And this was all the result of the pressure that was being exerted on the people. They were brought into the situation to request the approval to leave the territory of the municipality. There was a large number of non-Serbs from the territory of Sanski Most who worked elsewhere in the west as seasonal workers. They also had to sign such declaration so that their family would be able to leave for Croatia and third countries. And then there were lots of cases of simple evictions. People would be physically expelled from their homes, and Serb refugees, Serb war veterans would be given or allocated their homes, whereas the real owners had to live in some outside buildings or simply leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it was no secret. They had decided to allow less than 10 per cent of non-Serbs to remain in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I'm running short of time. I need to get to a couple more items if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we show the witness the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, this relates to what you were talking about, I believe. This is a document dated the 2nd of July, 1992, from the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P113.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I just want to read from Article number 1 under that decision entitled, "On the criteria for the possibility of the departure from the municipality." Article 1 says: "Voluntary departure from Sanski Most municipality shall be allowed. The families and persons who give a statement to the authorised municipal administration organ that they are permanently leaving the municipality and they're leaving their real property to Sanski Most municipality." Is that consistent with what you were aware of at that time as to the requirements for leaving Sanski Most by non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this -- that this was done, and during that period at the time I contacted the people of non-Serb ethnicity from the territory of the municipality, and they told me, yes, that this was indeed the case, that they had to sign the statement to the effect that they would never come back, that they would leave their property to the municipality of Sanski Most. They had to pay all of the arrears that they might have had, electricity, water bills, taxes, and all other dues that they had to pay. So it was just another way of extracting money from them. And see, for example, I had a beautiful house and I was evicted, physically evicted from my house, and a Serb national was brought to my house, and I would be forced outside, to live outside in an outhouse or a shed. And this is only one thing. This was coupled with numerous incidents of destruction and arson of the property belonging to those Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karabeg. I have two last items I want to show you before I finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could show the witness the next item, a photograph. This is ERN 02165297.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P114.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, you mentioned Betonirka and the prison where you were detained in Sanski Most. Were you aware of other facilities in town where non-Serbs were detained during that summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you name some of those?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, for instance, you have the Hasan Kikic school here, then the Krings hall, the sports centre -- or, rather, the gymnasium. It was quite typical for the schools to have been turned into camps where people were detained. There were other places as well. And I'm really sorry to this day that the memorial centre belonging to Simo Milusa, a famous revolutionary was used as a detention centre where people were interrogated, beaten up, and for that same reason that Hughes was burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that last question that was asked, placing a document in front of a witness with all the names there, I'm not entirely sure that that is of great use to the Trial Chamber, firstly. Secondly, whilst of course hearsay is accepted in the Tribunal, it's clearly not the best evidence in relation to this, and I just think a procedure whereby a document with a list of names is presented to the witness so he can read them out is -- is not effective evidence-taking, and I would object to that sort of evidence-taking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, yesterday we briefly discussed leading questions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may continue. I'd like to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To respond to the question, a specific question, and there's a correction that needs to be made. You see, here -- please. Please. Muhici is not a small town. Muhici is a street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I'll give you an opportunity to make whatever amendment or whatever change at a later stage. I first will respond to the objection to this question raised by Ms. Loukas. Mr. Hannis, yesterday we discussed leading questions, and you said, well, it was a yes or no question. Of course you could have asked on all the eight items on this photograph to see whether or not this was a detention facility. But just to clarify the issue, a leading question is a question which suggests the answer to be given or is a question which is based upon a not yet established fact. One could consider eight pictures of facilities of which already two of them have been identified as places where people were kept in detention, it would be suggestive for the other six. So it would have been appropriate to ask the witness whether he was aware of any other detention facilities and what was the basis of his knowledge if he was not detained there by himself. That would be a better way of introducing the matter than presenting eight pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, and I will take that in mind. I do want to indicate that my purpose in showing him this is just to try and verify that these eight separate locations pictured on here are accurately represented on the map as to their respective locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That might have been the next question, whether -- I think that Ms. Loukas would have less objections if we tried once the witness would have identified detection facilities where to put them on the map precisely because that's an easily verifiable issue. So I can imagine that she would not have objected against that leading issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In addition, Your Honour, a number of 92 bis statements of witnesses from this municipality have already been accepted into evidence and those witnesses talk about these detention facilities, and I was not aware that the Defence was seriously contesting that these were detention facilities in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed. But let me first give you an opportunity, Mr. Karabeg, to tell us what you'd like to tell us before the procedural incident was raised. Please tell me what you intended to say just a couple of minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I wanted to say: Mahala and Muhici, Mahala is a neighbourhood made up of several streets where the camps were. Muhici is just one street. It is one and a half kilometres long, but it's not -- that street could not have been a camp. Yes, in the street of Muhici and Gornja Mahala there were, but Gornja Mahala incorporates various quarters, a quarter of six or seven square hectares, in fact, a district of that size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You see, Ms. Loukas, that leading does not always lead to a confirmation of what the suggestion is, because the witness has now said that at least that some of these items, they could not as such have been detention facilities. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I just want to ask you with regard to those eight photographs on --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They couldn't be. Mahala couldn't be a whole neighbourhood. They had thousands of facilities. They wanted to knock it down and have a new town planning for their Serbs, the Serb soldiers to build a new settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, with regard to that photograph and map in front of you in that exhibit, I just want to ask you if the eight separate photographs which have a number 1 through 8 are accurately located on the map. Do you understand my question? Does each number correspond to the correct location for the photograph that pertains to that number?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. With the exception of this Muhic settlement, and Mahala settlement. I'm not quite clear on what that is. What does that mean? What is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there an area of Sanski Most town that was referred to as Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And we've just spoken about that, and it was five or six square hectares in size, in area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But Mahala is referred to as item number 7. Is the number 7 on the map in the correct general vicinity which was known as Mahala in Sanski Most town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to find my way here, the left and right bank. Mahala and Muhici were on the left bank of the Sana River. So I think so, yes. I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, may I ask you is there any specific relevance for the exact locations within Sanski Most for those facilities, and is there any dispute as to whether the SUP building was here or there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe it may help the Court in evaluating some of the written evidence of other witnesses. That's the only purpose that I'm offering it for at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is obviously no dispute about the locations of particular buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the location of these buildings might have been - apart from what they exactly were - might have been something that the parties could have agreed upon. Please proceed, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, now I want to show you one last item. If it could be given the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P115.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, this is a black-and-white photograph, and I would like you, if you can, identify any of the individuals in that photograph that you know and point them out to us or tell us where they're standing, what they look like.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Prior to there being any questioning in relation to the photograph, I think it's appropriate that a date might be established by the Prosecution. To see if it's in any way probative to this case before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would start if whether there's any -- whether the witness has any knowledge or whether you would -- whether or not in the presence of the witness would give us further information as to the time frame related to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can ask him a question about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you know how this photograph came to be here in court today? Have you seen this photograph before today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've seen this photograph before. This photograph was certainly taken on the 25th of May, 1992, until the 10th of October, 1995, taken in Sanski Most. Between that period of time certainly. I can't give you an exact date, but it was certainly taken between those dates, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I never saw Mr. Krajisnik. I never met him, but this is the period of time when I was not in Sanski Most myself. And the period I arrived in Sanski Most, when the liberation came, I came across this photograph in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I take it that was after the 10th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still not clear to me. Well, let's just assume. Why couldn't it be a photograph of 1989, for example?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you understand the question the Judge just asked?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. No, it cannot be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you explain why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can't be 1989 because I would know about it. I lived in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your answer suggests that the photograph is a photograph taken in Sanski Most. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know it was taken in Sanski Most because the guests, the head of the municipality, Nedeljko Rasula is here, for example. That's the head of the municipality that we've been talking about throughout, Nedeljko Rasula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it Mr. Rasula has been outside of Sanski Most now and then as well. What makes you accept that this is a picture taken in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of him. And it was found in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say it was taken in Sanski Most. Would it have been taken before I was arrested, I would have known about these persons together in Sanski Most, and you said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And after you were released or exchanged, you say you found -- did you personally find this photograph in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not personally. I took the photograph from a book, which was entitled, "It is a Crime to Forget a Crime."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seemed that it appeared on page 24. Perhaps you could ask. It's still not very conclusive, Mr. Hannis, to say the least, so if you would please further try to elaborate why perhaps in the framework of the book, whatever, to convince the Chamber that it is a relevant photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I may address that point first. What I wanted this witness to do was to identify the persons that he knows in the photograph, and at this point that's all I wanted to establish, the fact that particular individuals were together. Now, I don't have at this point additional information on the specifics as to what this event was and when exactly it occurred, but that may come in later. But with this witness, because he's the one that brought the photograph here, I wanted to ask him if he could identify a particular individual in that photograph. And the Defence objections and the other objections I think are matters that go to weight and something the Court may consider once you've heard all the other evidence regarding this municipality and this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say that what you want to establish at this very moment, awaiting what evidence further will be adduced, is that these persons have been photographed when being together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wherever, at whatever time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then to -- for this limited purpose, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, can you now tell us which individuals, if any, you recognise in the photograph and point them out for me and the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, this is the president, Nedeljko Rasula, president of the municipality of Sanski Most, Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, the witness is pointing to the gentleman in the middle of the photograph who is facing outward.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Toward the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to his immediate left, do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: To his immediate left is Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And seated at the table, do you recognise any of those people?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I recognise Karadzic and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for the record, he indicated the gentleman seated on the right side of the photograph and the woman to his immediate right. Left on the photograph but to the right of the individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Anyone else, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Ms. Loukas, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps after the break or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we take the break a bit earlier now and then you would have another 70 minutes remaining. We will adjourn until 25 minutes to 1.00, and there is any news about the documents we referred to earlier, Mr. Hannis, the Chamber would like to hear. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, any clarifications in respect of the source of the document and the circles around number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have now a different English translation. Actually, the English reads just the same except it has no handwriting on it, no circling, no underlining. This is the English translation of the ERN, the B/C/S original 00471274 through 1277, and I would now propose to offer to the Court to substitute this for the English translation that we had earlier with the circles and the underlining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there was a second issue about the provenance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. The information I have regarding that at this time, Your Honour, is this document was part of a package of documents received from AID in Bosnia in November of 1995. As you mentioned before, it has the name and the certification of the ICTY investigator who received the documents. The note that I've been able to find so far relating to that reads as follows, if I may, Your Honour: "In total this file contains 28 documents covering the period from 21 April 1992 to 23 June 1992." I don't have any other information internally from AID as to who in AID who found it, who they received it from, et cetera. I will try to get that information, but this is all I have at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll delay any decision until such information has been provided to the Chamber, of course unless the Defence would be satisfied by the explanation as given until now, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, actually I'd like to know a little further. And that objection in relation to the question of provenance, I think that was Exhibit number 111 applies also in relation to 112 and 113.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm just interested in the actual source, the original source of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: In question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, part of our argument is the original source of the document is the Sanski Most Crisis Staff, and some of those documents have a signature of the person. For example, I think one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One much them has. One of them is signed the Crisis Staff. But of course what Ms. Loukas is referring to is how did it get from the Sanski Most Crisis Staff to AID, if it ever came from Sanski Most Crisis Staff. We'll delay decision on this, but it has been -- we have taken notice that an objection is made in that respect. Ms. Loukas, then, may I invite you to start cross-examination of the witness. You'll now be examined by counsel for the Defence, Ms. Loukas. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, of course you've previously given evidence before this Tribunal in the Brdjanin and Talic case, the case against Mr. Brdjanin and the late Mr. Talic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- and I think you gave that evidence between the dates of the 27th of May, 2002, and the 30th of May, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course prior to giving your evidence, you gave the solemn declaration that you would tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I formally tender the transcript of the previous cross-examination under 92 bis (D).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would then be, as far as I can see it, pages 6208 up till and including of those stricken out, 6313.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. There were just some irrelevant matters on that last page there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, what I propose to do firstly is just take you to your statement that is now in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps it might be useful if the copy of Mr. Karabeg's statement with the numbered paragraphs was placed in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you have that statement before you now, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Lovely. Now, I just want to highlight some of the matters there briefly that are contained within your statement. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And this hopefully should be a relatively simple process with hopefully most of the questions being able to be answered yes or no. Now, firstly I take you to paragraph 11 of your statement, and you see there that you've stated there: "I do not have firsthand information of the functions of the Crisis Staff, and all I know is only hearsay and rumours." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, obviously as a lawyer, you're very careful about ensuring the accuracy of matters that you put in your legal statement, and that's why you've fairly mentioned that matter there in paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, going to paragraph 39 of your statement. Do you have that before you there, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And it's there stated that in relation -- I think you indicate there was a pleasant meeting, and then there was further stated that there would be no meeting, but the point you make there, the point I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. want to emphasise there is the SDS told you that they could not control their extremists. That's correct, and that's what you have stated there, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you require just yes or no answers or may I give broader explanations and answers?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I want you to confirm for me that the SDS stated to you that they could not control their extremists.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Right. And that's all I'm seeking your agreement to at this stage, the matters that are covered in your statement. You understand that aspect, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: One of the negotiators was Tomo Delic, and he led the SOS, and he said to us that he could not rein in the extremists, whereas he was the head of the extremists. And it is true that that is what they said. That is true, yes. But he was at the head of the extremists, Delic, for instance, and his cafe was his property, and he said that he can't -- could not control those people under his command, in actual fact, but it's true that they said yes, they could not control their extremists.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the name Tomo Delic, but of course the situation is that it wasn't just Tomo Delic telling you that SDS could not control their extremists?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Tomo said that and so did Boro Savanovic and Vlado Vrkes. Vlado Vrkes even cried. Cried right in front of us. He shed a tear and asked us, entreated us to leave the municipality building but nothing happened that actual evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving on to paragraph 56 of your statement. Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 56, you state, of course, that you had no dealings with the SOS and that you further state there, further down in the paragraph, that you believed that the SDS funded the SOS because you saw them together several times. You see that aspect in your paragraph there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, of course, and being entirely fair, I think you've indicated there in that paragraph that it was, of course, your -- it was just your belief that the SDS was associated with the SOS.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: You can translate the term "belief" in any way you like, but that was the situation at that time. They were all the same, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But you fairly state in your statement that that's your belief.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm now claiming. I might have said believe then, but I now say I claim after all the knowledge I have had afterwards about that period and talking to the Serbs who returned to Sanski Most and who live in Sanski Most today, having returned to their own houses. So let me repeat: It is possible that I used the verb "to believe" then, but I now claim and assert.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you claim and assert on the basis of things you've heard from other people subsequently. That would be a fair statement of what you're saying, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: After such a long period of time and what I learnt about it, and a lot was learnt about it later on, and if I was to make a statement here and now today, I would give a different statement, a more specific and concrete statement, because I learnt more on the basis of talking to people, documents and so on and so forth. So my statement today would be different than it was then.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Karabeg, this statement -- you gave this statement in July 1999, I think. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you've had the opportunity to make further corrections in relation to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this: If I were to correct --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: First of all, you have had the opportunity to correct your statement. Firstly answer my question and then we can go on to other aspects.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. And if I were to correct them further, I would correct them on a daily basis, every day, because I always learn more and hear about more things.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So basically you're saying you believed then but your own opinion is that you're convinced now. That would be a fair assessment of what you're saying, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would, yes, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, if you'd just turn to paragraph 70 of your statement. You've stated there that: "During this first time in the prison, prisoners were taken out for interrogation and beaten. The guards, soldiers, police and even people from the street would come and beat prisoners." You see that particular aspect there at paragraph 70, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, you'd agree with me it all sounds a little chaotic, the situation there whereby people are just coming in from the street and beating prisoners? It sounds like there was quite some situation of chaos. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just going to paragraph 76. You of course there quite -- indicate that you never saw any Serb leaders at Betonirka camp, and that's of course correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And that further in relation, I think, to paragraph 83, if you might turn to that particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There were no women there. And I think paragraph 84, that -- sorry, paragraph 87, that you never saw any men die or any dead bodies at Betonirka. That's what you've stated there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course that's all true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the truth. I never said it wasn't the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No. This process, I'm just getting you to confirm particular aspects of your written statement at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one small clarification to the witness. Mr. Karabeg, in line 83, the English translation -- in paragraph 83, the English translation reads: "While I was in Betonirka, there were no women that he saw kept in the camp." Does this mean that you never saw a woman kept detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I did not see that. But I can't claim whether there were any or not. I simply didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So when you confirmed on the question of Ms. Loukas whether -- that it was true that there were no women in the camp, your answer correctly is that you never saw any women being kept detained in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I did not see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. So we've confirmed that aspect of paragraph 83 and paragraph 87. Now, I'm just going to switch areas now, Mr. Karabeg, and I just want to take you to certain aspects of your previous testimony when you gave evidence in the case against Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Talic, the late Mr. Talic. Now, firstly, Mr. Karabeg, taking you to -- for the benefit of the Court, I'm going to page 6210 of the transcript. Now, just in relation to that, Mr. Karabeg, I'll read through some of the questions and answers you gave there and just ask you to confirm those particular answers. Firstly you were asked this question -- and I think I can go a little bit more quickly, Your Honour, because the interpreters do have copies of this particular transcript before them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but they have to translate into B/C/S, and they might not have a B/C/S transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I better clarify that. I assumed that the interpreters had copies of the transcripts, but perhaps they don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But apart from that, that would be the English transcript only.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would read slowly, because having the original is not yet providing a translation into B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, it might be easier for them to have one, but if you start reading slowly -- there are copies I do understand. Yes. If they could be distributed to the -- how many copies do we have? One. Yes, and that's for the English, B/C/S booth then I take it. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, now, just going to page 6210, you were asked this particular question when you were being cross-examined by Ms. Fauveau-Ivanovic. You recall that aspect of that particular cross-examination, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You were asked this question: "Prior to the elections of 1990, Sanski Most municipality was indeed part of the association of Banja Luka municipalities." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I'm having trouble hearing the -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. So you were asked this question. And your response was: "Yes, indeed. Bosanska Krajina." Do you recall that question and answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course that's true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And the municipalities which you have just named, Kljuc, Prijedor, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanska Gradska, Celinac, Latasi, were also municipalities that were part of the association of Banja Luka municipalities or, as you say, as you call it, Bosanska Krajina. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And your answer was, of course: "Yes, that's the way it was. Bosnia and Herzegovina was divided into these regions. That was within the framework of Yugoslavia." Now, the other aspect I wanted to ask you in relation to that particular portion of the cross-examination is that -- for the benefit of the Court at page 6244 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Does everybody have that particular page?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you were asked this question: "Yesterday you said that you saw General Talic on television cordially greeting leaders of the SDS; is that correct?" And your answer was: "Yes, and he was in the front row. The camera shot a close-up of those people." And of course that is an aspect of which you gave evidence earlier today. You recall that, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: You were further asked this question: "The occasion at which General Talic was with the SDS leaders was this celebration of the liberation of Banja Luka at the end of the Second World War, was it not?" And your answer was: "I think it was. I think it was."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you were further asked this question: "And that celebration was held every year, was it not? Even before 1990, these celebrations were a regular event. Isn't that so?"

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And your answer was: "I think so. We had similar celebrations in Sanski Most, the 20th of October, which was celebrated every year. So I assume that was what had happened in Banja Luka. I can't claim that because I didn't go there." Do you agree with the response you've given there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And, of course, just in relation to that particular aspect, is it possible you're mistaken about seeing Mr. Krajisnik on that -- when you saw it on the TV?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, first are you referring to my answer yesterday, the one I gave yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to the evidence you've given globally in relation to this issue, that you spoke about, I think -- you gave evidence about this aspect previously when you gave evidence in the Brdjanin case, and I think it was today --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the answer that I gave. But at that time, I was primarily interested in General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. So you couldn't be certain that you saw Mr. Krajisnik on that particular occasion on the television footage that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw that, and I maintain that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. So what date are you saying this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a lot, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm just asking approximately.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- this was -- we parted with General Talic on the 20th of April, 1992, on Monday. I didn't call him on Tuesday. I called him on Wednesday. So this could have been either on Thursday or Friday. Monday, the 20th or Tuesday the 21st. Either the 23rd or the 24th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you're talking about April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now -- and I'm putting to you that you're mistaken about Mr. Krajisnik being there in April 1992. What do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That's -- that's your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that you're mistaken about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, at that time I wasn't paying much attention on them. I focused on General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Karabeg, you see, Mr. Krajisnik was not there in 1992, in April 1992, so is it just possible that what you saw on TV was file footage from another year?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, again I did not pay much attention to that. That footage showed me that those who were destructive and who were perpetrating crimes were there, and General Talic was with them. General Talic who had promised that he would take care of the situation, that there be would peace, and there he was sitting in the front row with the people who were destroying Bosnia-Herzegovina. And on that footage -- it's not that I saw anything bad, anything evil. I just saw General Talic with those people, which made me realise that he would not make good to the promises that he had given and that it was merely for the sake of appearances that he had come to Sanski Most and talked to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But again as you fairly conceded, Mr. Karabeg, you couldn't be certain that Mr. Krajisnik was there because your emphasis was on the fact that you saw General Talic there? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed him, I noticed Karadzic, and I noticed Plavsic. And another civilian -- I'm sorry, and the priest whose name now escapes me. The local priest, I noticed him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, could you -- or I would ask the witness. Your answer was -- you were asked whether -- that you couldn't be certain that Mr. Krajisnik was there because your emphasis was on the fact that you saw General Talic there, that's correct, isn't it, and you said, "I noticed him." I understood this to be General Talic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, at that time my attention was focused on General Talic and who he was with. He was there with those who were destroying Bosnia and Herzegovina. And on the other hand, he had come to see us to talk about peace and improving the situation, and it was when I saw the footage that I concluded that he would not make good on his promises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's your appreciation of the situation, and we are mainly focusing now on the exact facts. That means when you said, "I noticed him, I noticed Karadzic, I noticed Plavsic and another civilian," you referred to the priest. You meant by "him" you meant General Talic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant and I also noticed Krajisnik. I was referring to him as well. I was referring to Krajisnik, Talic, Plavsic, and Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas. And I'm not asking you to move to your next subject, because I can imagine that you will have some further questions on this issue as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: As a result of Your Honour's question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. But again, Mr. Karabeg, it's correct to say, is it not, that you could be mistaken about seeing Mr. Krajisnik on this particular file footage because your emphasis was on General Talic? That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour. I need to object to that question because I don't think there's any evidence yet that it was file footage, and he's already answered the question about whether he could be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I'll withdraw that, Your Honour. I was thinking about the file footage, but it's obviously the TV --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It still has to be established. That's one of the examples of leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, what you saw on TV that you've given evidence about previously, I'm putting to you that to be absolutely fair, you would concede that it's possible you were mistaken about seeing Mr. Krajisnik on TV because your emphasis was, of course, on General Talic and General Talic was your focus because you'd just been dealing with him in the days prior to your watching this television footage?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I noticed the people who were present there, and I also saw that General Talic was in their company, and I realised immediately that the whole thing was a lie, because there was nothing essentially bad about this ceremony, the liberation of the town of Banja Luka. Quite the contrary. It's a very fine occasion to celebrate the day that municipality was liberated. Again, I didn't see anything wrong with that. I just concluded that because of the company he was in, he had lied to us, that he would not do what he had promised to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, may I stop you here. It's entirely clear what your thoughts were and what your appreciation was at that time seeing Mr. Talic on television. But that's not the issue we're discussing at this moment. This morning, and I literally quote to you, you said: "I saw Talic sitting in the front row together with Karadzic. I believe Krajisnik was also there together with Biljana Plavsic and others, and because of that I only laughed at what they had said." The issue is this morning you said, "I saw Talic together with Karadzic. I believe Krajisnik was also there." The question is: This morning you said, "I believe Krajisnik was there," and you seem to be more certain now, a couple of hours later. The question is: Why did you say this morning "I believed" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But let me -- let me tell you. I said this morning, and what I said this morning I abide by that, but the lady from the Defence insisting on something. I don't know exactly what she's insisting on. Maybe she wants me to also leave out "I think" or "I believe," that it was an old file TV footage. How would I know that? But I maintain -- I abide by what I said initially. I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a second question, whether you saw on television the footage of what happened that day or whether you saw on television any footage of something that happened before, one year before or at any other occasion. The question is where you said this morning, unless you say, "I didn't say that," and we'll check that in the original audiotape, where you said this morning, "I believe Krajisnik was there together with Plavsic." You seem to be more certain at this moment. We would like to know why did you say "I believe" this morning and why do you now say, "I saw him on television"? And I'm talking about Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it's -- it's -- it's self-implying, because I believe I saw him means that I saw him. If I said that I believed I saw him, it means that I had probably seen him there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say it's a probability that you saw him that day appearing on television. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karabeg, you fairly conceded to his Honour that it's a probability that you saw him that day appearing on television. So clearly you can see the possibility that you didn't see him that day on television?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot acknowledge that, that it is possible that I did not see him on that day. I don't accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, leaving that aside, are you prepared to concede the possibility that you are mistaken about it being current footage, as at that time, April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I think he already answered the question that he wouldn't have any way of knowing whether or not it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was file footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think Ms. Loukas is entitled to further explore whether this absence of any knowledge is well-founded. Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Karabeg, I just am going to ask you that question again. Are you prepared to concede the possibility that you are mistaken about it being current footage at that time, April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question. I don't have a question to that answer -- I don't have an answer to that question. Correction. I didn't work in TV. I don't know how it was edited. I didn't see it -- I didn't see any writing to the effect that it was a file footage. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karabeg, so the question is whether you had any positive reason to accept that it was a footage from the same day or whether there was any indication that it would not be the footage of something that happened that same day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a reason, because it is quite possible that the TV broadcast what was happening on that day, because otherwise something would have been written on the image to the effect that it was a file footage or archives or a date. It was a simple gathering or a simple rally that took place on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but there was nothing like, for example, the weather or -- well, whatever that gave you the impression that it was the footage of what happened that same day or any reference made by any of the speakers to what happened the day before or a week before which could not have been said one year earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. There was the TV presenter who said that on that day, a ceremony was held on account of the anniversary of the liberation of Banja Luka and that present were so-and-so, a couple of -- several of them, and then this footage from the ceremony was shown. I don't know what it was exactly, whether it was a session in -- whether it was inside the hall. There were dozens of people there, but I don't exactly know what kind of ceremony it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it was a footage shown during a news programme or any programme --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During a news programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, moving on to another area. Page 6251 of the transcript, for the Court's benefit. You were asked some questions there and gave answers I just want to confirm with you, Mr. Karabeg. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, these questions were asked: "Hence you don't know exactly what happened in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje during your detention. Is this accurate?" And your answer was: "Well, I heard it from others, what the others experienced, but I personally never saw it." Do you remember that portion of the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do, because I had already been imprisoned. So it was not possible for me to see what was happening in Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Karabeg. Now, the next question that was asked: "The persons who told you about what happened, did they tell you that the Muslims arrested 46 Serbian officers in that place?" And your answer was: "Yes." And the next question was: "Did they tell you that the persons who arrested these Serbian officers were armed?" And your answer was: "Yes." And the next question was: "Therefore you aware of the fact that there was fighting going on in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo." And your answer was: "Yes, I am." You recall that aspect of the cross-examination, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving along to another aspect of the cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, may I ask you one thing. On page 6250.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Reference is made to the statement about the -- the testimony about murders taking place in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje. That was in chief, wasn't it? So the Chamber might have some difficulties in finding the right time frame for that. So if you would perhaps provide the Chamber with the relevant page or pages where this statement is made, because it's in response of what he testified.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Yes, I'll attend to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I won't be able to attend to that right this moment, but I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, moving along to page 6274 of the cross-examination, for the Court's benefit. Sorry, no. That's pages 6280. Now, you were also asked some questions there about Mr. Vrkes, and I'll just read you out the questions and answers and then I'll ask you some questions about it, Mr. Karabeg: "Okay. You were talking yesterday about Mr. Vrkes mentioning a couple of names to you, Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Krajisnik when he talked about the pressures being put on him from Banja Luka for Sanski Most to join the Banja Luka region. You, of course, have no idea whether Mr. Vrkes was telling you the truth; correct?" And your answer was: "Well, let me see. No." Your next question was -- the next question you were asked was: "He may have just done that as an excuse for what he was planning to do regarding joining Sanski Most with that association. In other words, blaming it on someone else besides himself. That's a possibility, isn't it?" And you were answer was, "It's possible. It's possible. It's possible." You recall that aspect of the cross-examination, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And that was, of course, true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And there was a further short question where I think Mr. Ackerman said: "Now?" And your answer was: "I beg your pardon? I'm conveying to you what he said. I didn't say that I personally spoke to that gentleman but that he said that they were exposed to pressure" -- sorry, I'm going a bit fast. "I beg your pardon. I'm conveying to you what he said. I didn't say that I personally spoke to that gentleman but that he said they were exposed to pressure, so it is possible." That's now been translated to you, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What has been translated to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your answer.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. Yes. Yes. Yes. I thought that you said that something else has been translated to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So, of course, you've there fairly conceded that you don't know, of course, whether Mr. Vrkes was telling the truth, and you concede fairly that it's possible he was just using the names as an excuse. That's correct, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, before you move to your next subject, on page 6281, third line, "Gentleman" is in the single. It makes more sense to be in the plural. How did you understand this to be, that "Gentleman," whether it was a person or the two persons mentioned before? Because the names mentioned were Brdjanin and Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry. My microphone's off. Well, Your Honour, I think it's clear that in his last answer to me that he's encapsulating both gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's why I went on to ask the additional question, because I thought it needed some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, just a few other matters I'd like to cover with you, Mr. Karabeg. Of course, you gave a rather long statement to the Prosecution back in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And -- and of course as a lawyer, you're aware of the importance of the statements that are taken by Prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And you're also aware of course, of the importance of accuracy and honesty in the statements?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course of trying to ensure that you put in everything you know about a particular situation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course that statement you gave back in 1999 took about two days, I think, to give.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long it took.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: All right. So you don't really recall how long it took back in 1999? Well, of course the dates on the statement are 24th to the 25th of July, Mr. Karabeg. So you're basically saying you don't know how many hours you spent per day doing the statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, no, because it was all five years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course. Now -- and, of course, I think prior to giving that --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
